ops.content: The brain daemon restart protocol now routes through `launchctl kickstart -k` rather than a direct Popen spawn. When a restart is needed, the caller invokes `launchctl kickstart -k <service-target>`, which causes launchd to tear down the existing daemon process and immediately relaunch it under the managed service definition. This ensures the daemon inherits the correct environment, resource limits, and sandbox profile defined in the launchd plist, and that launchd owns the process lifecycle (crash recovery, log routing, etc.). Direct Popen spawning is no longer used and should not be reintroduced.

ops.content: The brain daemon restart protocol now routes through `launchctl kickstart -k` rather than a direct Popen spawn. When a restart is needed, the controlling process invokes `launchctl kickstart -k gui/<UID>/com.brain.daemon` (or equivalent service label), which instructs launchd to immediately stop the running instance and relaunch it under launchd's supervision. This ensures the daemon inherits the correct environment, respects plist-defined resource limits, and is automatically re-supervised after crashes — properties that the old direct-spawn approach did not guarantee.

ops.title: WAL checkpoint starvation under parallel sessions
ops.content: When two sessions write concurrently, the TRUNCATE checkpoint starves; symptom is an ever-growing -wal file.

connect_to.title: e5f6a7b8
connect_to.why: Checkpoint starvation is a direct downstream effect of writer-slot contention: when two sessions compete for the WAL writer slot, the TRUNCATE checkpoint cannot complete, causing the -wal file to grow unboundedly.
